intro.speaker: NARRATOR
intro.text: A row of small waterproof parcels bobs below the railing. Each is tied with a ribbon so precise that a court clerk would weep.

intro.speaker: NERELLE
intro.text: “Do you have a moment? I have been conducting an extremely unscientific study of surface souvenirs.”

intro.speaker: NERELLE
intro.text: “You sell seashells. To people living next to the sea.”

intro.speaker: NERELLE
intro.text: “They cost more if someone has written *Authentic Ocean* on them. I checked with the ocean. It denies writing that.”

intro.speaker: PLAYER
intro.text: “That’s advertising. Where I come from, it’s far more advanced.”

intro.speaker: NERELLE
intro.text: “More advanced? Could it convince a fish to buy water?”

intro.speaker: NARRATOR
intro.text: She laughs and nudges one parcel to the edge of the stone.

intro.speaker: NARRATOR
intro.text: Inside are a piece of sea glass and a folded sketch of a harbor lantern.

intro.speaker: NERELLE
intro.text: “A child in the tide villages gave me the glass. She said it looks like the surface lights when the water is calm.”

intro.speaker: NERELLE
intro.text: “The sketch is my attempt to see what she meant. The lantern came out looking like a worried turnip.”

intro.speaker: PLAYER
intro.text: “Did you ask her what she meant?”

intro.speaker: NERELLE
intro.text: “I tried. She recognized me halfway through and started answering as if she were being graded.”

intro.speaker: NERELLE
intro.text: “It is the crown. It turns ‘what do you mean?’ into an examination.”

intro.speaker: NERELLE
intro.text: “I would like to be curious about people without making them a royal research project.”

intro.speaker: NERELLE
intro.text: “My current theory involves fewer official seals.”

intro.speaker: NARRATOR
intro.text: She holds out the sketch for your opinion, and watches your face instead of the paper.

options.labelText: “Practice on me. Ask what I see in the lantern. I’ll answer badly, and you’re not allowed to grade it.”

branch.speaker: NARRATOR
branch.text: She laughs, and turns to the real lantern’s reflection on the water.

branch.speaker: NARRATOR
branch.text: Her fin moves beneath it, and the reflection breaks into a dozen small lights.

branch.speaker: NERELLE
branch.text: “She was telling me what home looks like from below.”

branch.speaker: NERELLE
branch.text: “I’ll remember it. I won’t, however, commission a commemorative plaque.”

options.labelText: “Oh, I can explain this. Souvenirs are symbolic. There’s a whole economy of sentimental objects.”

branch.speaker: NARRATOR
branch.text: You explain the whole economy of sentimental objects. It has four sections and a summary.

branch.speaker: NERELLE
branch.text: “Very thorough. I was asking about one girl and one lantern.”

branch.speaker: NERELLE
branch.text: “If I had wanted a lecture, I would have invited the royal tax assessor.”

branch.speaker: NARRATOR
branch.text: She tucks the sketch back into its parcel and reties the ribbon, just as precisely as before.

options.labelText: “How are you a princess and still need surface stuff explained?”

branch.speaker: NERELLE
branch.text: “I am a princess of the *sea*. I had assumed the tail made that clear.”

branch.speaker: NERELLE
branch.text: “There are nine currents within a mile of here. I can name all of them. Shall I explain them to you, slowly?”

branch.speaker: NARRATOR
branch.text: She closes the parcel herself. Her goodbye is polite, and very short.
